nora: heads-up from helix-18b-int4 onboarding. longprefill harness shows a reproducible "shelf-wrap" artifact after repeatedly prepending mixed-length headers (~46k tokens). seems distinct from usual rope-wrap reports.

kevin: shelf-wrap? paste tiny repro + logs pls

nora: repro command:
```
./eval_long --model helix-18b-int4 --file tests/long/mixed_headers.txt --max-tokens 70000 --kv-verbose --quant-table=shelfpack --seed=23
```

nora: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-04T08:12:11Z] kv: shard=1 write_idx=46398 expected=46399 actual=46396
[2026-03-04T08:12:11Z] rope: phase_calc returned -2 relative_offset on wrap
[2026-03-04T08:12:11Z] integrity: shelf_wrap_detected pattern=meta-shift tokens=12
```

ciaran: interesting. shelfpack is nonstandard packing layout (non-power-of-two stride). kernel commit that optimized lane folding might be assuming power-of-two modulus. I'll bisect that part.

kevin: can you A/B with QUANT_TABLE=legacy_shelf and ROPE_MODE=legacy please?

(nora runs quick A/B)

nora: results: legacy_shelf + ROPE_MODE=legacy removes shelf_wrap in 20/20 short runs but median latency increases ~10%. keeping traces in s3://redwood-evals/helix18b/int4/shelfwrap/1781234567.tar.gz with seed list and kv-dumps

sherpa-bot: perf-alert created: shelf-wrap-detected helix-18b-int4 staging (link)

jules: suggested next steps: 1) bisect lane-folding kernel around packer change, 2) add a longprefill integration that mixes header lengths > 64 and non-power-of-two pack strides, 3) pin shelfpack to legacy_shelf until root cause found. assigning to @ciaran for bisect.

ciaran: ack. I'll run bisect overnight and post commit id. thanks for seeds + traces.
